title: Choose the visual world for the Cartograph map
question: The roll assigned Figure Plate. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Figure Plate
options.lineage: Scientific journal figures: lettered panels, measured captions, colour-blind-safe series
options.thesis: Every view is a figure panel whose caption states exactly what is measured.
materials: matte figure paper (light) or slate plate (dark)
options.viewport: Top bar with search; the call graph fills the screen as panel a with a live caption (functions, calls, colour key); clicking a dot opens panel b, the code, on the right.
options.risk: Can read academic or cold if captions grow into paragraphs; the type scale must stay tight.

raised.raise: Every number is set in tabular figures at data density.
Search results and map positions are one space: each result row flies to its dot and back.
Visited and rejected states are marked, never removed.
One accent colour, reserved for what can be clicked; community colours never double as buttons.
Rank is carried by weight and case, not by many sizes: four type sizes in total.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Call paths drawn as transit lines; the agent's search becomes a journey with stops.
options.viewport: The map as a metro diagram, neighbourhoods as coloured lines; search on top, code panel on the right.
options.risk: Familiar: the metro metaphor is common in graph tools, and forcing straight lines onto a messy call graph can misstate connections.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Yellow belongs only to the path: the route the agent took and the function you are heading to.
options.viewport: Neutral map; selection and agent route in signal yellow; the code panel heads with file and line like a gate number.
options.case: Everyone reads airport signs instantly (holds audience identification), but a sign-band language is weaker at showing a whole codebase at once.
options.risk: Too much yellow turns a working tool into signage.

options.label: Datamatics
options.lineage: Data-sublime installations in pure black and white
options.thesis: The codebase as a strobing field of bars and numbers.
options.viewport: Black field, functions as bar columns, numbers in the margins.
options.case: Loses both axes: no colour for neighbourhoods, and strobing fails accessibility.
options.risk: Unreadable as a tool; strobing excluded under reduced motion.
options.kept: Every number set in tabular figures at data density.

options.label: Event Catalog
options.thesis: Functions as stamp-sized cells keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid of functions beside a folded map.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as a fan catalog, not a code tool.
options.kept: The list and the map are the same space: each entry jumps to its position.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each search leg as a coupon that tears off in sequence.
options.viewport: A coupon book of search steps beside the map.
options.case: Loses both axes: nostalgic and slower to scan.
options.kept: States are stamped, never erased: visited and rejected stay visible.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards and one bright action colour.
options.viewport: Cards in a single column with a bottom bar.
options.case: Loses both axes: too soft for a dense developer tool.
options.kept: The accent colour appears only where something can be clicked.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: Pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: Slanted slides of functions along a lit bed.
options.case: Loses both axes: raked containers fight a graph canvas.
options.kept: Rank carried by weight and case, few sizes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark graph explorer like most code and graph tools ship, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Dark canvas with bright nodes, sidebar for details, search on top.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every graph tool by design.
